newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - TRI 1996 net up 36 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - TRI 1996 net up 36 pct.

text.p: Following is a sample of views on the results of Malaysian telecommunications company Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) for the year to December 31, 1996.
The company reported a net profit of 251.01 million ringgit, compared to 185.01 million in 1995.
GREG FELDBERG, TELECOMMUNICATIONS ANALYST AT H.G. ASIA'

"We were expecting a net profit of 248.6 million ringgit, so the actual figure of 251.01 million was essentially in line with our forecast. It is also close to the consensus view, so the result should be seen as positive."
HAIZAN KHIR, TELECOMMUNICATIONS ANALYST AT SCHRODERS
"One point of concern is the higher-than-expected depreciation cost of 50 million ringgit. Also the tax charge is higher than we expected.
"Overall the profits were within expectations, and we are not changing any of our views on the stock. It is still an underperforming stock.
"The market has priced TRI fairly over the past few days."
SIMONE YEOH, TELECOMMUNICATIONS ANALYST, HSBC JAMES CAPEL
"The net profit figure was essentially in line, but the turnover and the pre tax figures were about 13 to 14 percent higher than expected.
"This is because the second half tax rate was substantially higher at 34 percent, which is near corporate rates. The rate for the first half was around 23 percent.
"The (net profit) figure could be viewed as slightly positive. Operationally it looks better than expected.
"The share price on Monday could stay at current levels or it could move slightly higher."
